title: miStudio result language, v1
description: The suite's result language: the fields every suite tool's result may carry (approval, next_steps, unavailable with its reason), the error body and its text format, miAssist's own result shape, and the MCP annotation rules every suite server's tests read. Owned by miAssist; consumers vendor this file byte-identical. Generated by scripts/write_contracts.py; do not edit.

x-error-text-format.description: An error's text: line 1 is "<code>: <one-line message>", line 2 "fix: <text>", line 3 "next: <JSON list of next_step>" (one line, "[]" when there is none), then the original text unchanged (an app error's own message; omitted for miAssist's own errors when it would repeat line 1). An app's code in any other case is lower-cased for line 1 and keeps its spelling in the original text.
x-error-text-format.groups: Each pattern's first group is the value; line 1's are the code, then the message.
x-error-text-format.rest: The original text, unchanged; omitted when it would repeat line 1.

x-annotation-rules.rule: Every tool has a non-empty title.
Every tool sets readOnlyHint and destructiveHint explicitly.

Read-only means the tool changes nothing: it starts no job, GPU or model call, files no approval, spends no paid call, and writes no row, file or artifact; any other tool has readOnlyHint false. The HTTP method does not decide it: a POST that changes nothing (no row, job, approval, file or paid call) is read-only, and a POST that starts a worker task is not.

Destructive means the tool deletes, purges, clears or cancels, changes served weights in place, or changes a setting that enables later deletion; such a tool has destructiveHint true, every other tool false.
A tool whose result has a typed shape declares an outputSchema; untyped results are listed as debt.
A relay carries its source tool's hints only when its REST call set equals the source tool's; otherwise AR-3 and AR-4 apply to the relay's own calls (a GET-only relay stays read-only).

app_id.description: One of the suite's four apps.

approval_status.description: Where an approval stands. miWorkbench's caller-executed routes map `consumed` to `executed` and `denied` to `rejected`; the server-executed apps use these words as they are and never `approved`.

approval.description: An action waiting for an app's operator. Only the operator decides it, in the app named by `decide_in`; the caller cannot approve it.

id.description: The deciding app's own approval id.

then.description: server_runs: the app runs the action itself once approved. call_again_with: the caller makes the call in call_again_with once approved.

reason.description: Why it was rejected, failed or expired, when known.

call_again.description: The call to make again once an approval is approved (caller-executed routes).

next_step.description: A suggested call: a tool on the server that emitted the result, with its arguments and the reason to make it.

unavailable.description: A dependency that could not be reached, named, with the reason.

error_body.description: An error: a code, a one-line message, the fix, and the next steps (possibly none).

error_code.description: An error code: lower case, one optional dotted app prefix, at most 64 characters. An app's own code in any other case is lower-cased here and keeps its spelling in the original text.

explanation.description: miAssist's plain-words explanation of a result, at the person's guidance level.

terms.description: Glossary keys of the terms the explanation uses.

assist_result.description: The structured result of every miAssist tool.

guidance.description: The guidance level a result was rendered at.

result_fields.description: The fields any suite tool's result may carry beside its own. An app's own fields stay (`additionalProperties` is true); an app's legacy `next` key is untouched and unconstrained: `next_steps` is the contract's key.
